record.original_question: Conjecture: If G is a transitive permutation group on a finite set Ω, then for any distinct α, β in Ω there is an element g ∈ G with αg = β whose number of fixed points is different from 1. P. Müller

evidence.quote: Conjecture: If G is a transitive permutation group on a finite set Ω, then for any distinct α, β in Ω there is an element g ∈ G with αg = β whose number of fixed points is different from 1. P. Müller

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let G be a transitive permutation group acting on a finite set Ω, and for g ∈ G let fix(g) = |{x ∈ Ω : g(x) = x}| denote its number of fixed points. Prove or disprove the following: for every pair of distinct points α, β ∈ Ω, there exists an element g ∈ G with g(α) = β such that fix(g) ≠ 1.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears as a newly posed problem in the 2026 edition of the Kourovka Notebook, attributed to P. Müller. Web searches did not surface any published proof or counterexample, and related results on fixed points in transitive permutation groups (e.g., Peter Neumann's conjecture, Burness–Hall on almost elusive groups) treat related but distinct questions. The problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Kourovka Notebook of unsolved problems in group theory
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of unsolved problems in group theory, including problems on fixed points of permutations posed by various authors.
status_evidence.claim: The Kourovka Notebook collects newly posed open problems in group theory; the conjecture by P. Müller appears as a new entry.

status_evidence.title: On a conjecture of Peter Neumann on fixed points in permutation groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies fixed-point properties in transitive permutation groups, related to but distinct from Müller's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses adjacent fixed-point conjectures, with no resolution of Müller's specific statement found.
